body:

https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-branches-in-your-repository/renaming-a-branch
-->

Pre-ConfidentialKeyRotation, `MPTokenIssuanceSet` rejects any attempt to modify an existing `IssuerEncryptionKey`/`AuditorEncryptionKey`, and an auditor key can never be provided without the issuer key (`temMALFORMED` in preflight).

Post-ConfidentialKeyRotation:
1.  allow late-registering auditor key after issuance key already registered on ledger
2. prevent registering auditor key if issuance key is not already registered or not being registered in the same tx
3. allow late-registering auditor key even if COA > 0
4. allow rotating issuer key even if it already exists on ledger
5. allow rotating auditor key even if it already exists on ledger
6. allow rotating even if COA > 0


Epoch:
1. when not opt-in confidential, epoch absent
2. first time register key: epoch keeps absent, matching issuances whose keys were registered before the ConfidentialKeyRotation amendment.
3. rotating key: epoch + 1

title: fix: Correct and simplify Linux packaging
body:
Bug fixes:

- Restore the RPM's systemd and shadow-utils dependencies. %{?systemd_requires}
  and %{?sysusers_requires_compat} sat after %debug_package, which opens the
  debuginfo subpackage, so both were silently dropped and the package declared
  neither. On a host without systemd installed the package still installed, but
  %pre and %post created no xrpld user and no /var/lib/xrpld or /var/log/xrpld.
- Declare the DEB's real libc6 floor. dpkg-shlibdeps derived libc6 (>= 2.34)
  from the build host's symbols file, where sysconf carries that minver, while
  the binaries are built against glibc 2.31 and reference nothing above
  GLIBC_2.30. That locked out distros they run on, Ubuntu 20.04 among them.
  debian/rules now rewrites the bound to LIBC_MIN and fails the build if either
  binary outgrows it.
- Ship LICENSE.md in the DEB. It was staged and installed by the RPM, but
  missing from debian/xrpld.docs, so it never reached the package.
- Own /usr/share/doc/xrpld in the RPM. Installing the docs by absolute path
  skips rpm's implicit ownership of the directory.
- Replace %build_mtime_policy with %clamp_mtime_to_source_date_epoch. The
  former is undefined on rpm 4.19 (AlmaLinux 10, the packaging image), so the
  line was a no-op and the clamping came from the redhat-rpm-config default.
- Make the RPM reproducible with %use_source_date_epoch_as_buildtime and a
  pinned %_buildhost. Without them the header records the wall clock and the
  build container's hostname, so two builds of the same commit differed. The
  DEB was already byte-identical on a rebuild.
- Pin the mode of /etc/xrpld with %attr, so the buildroot's umask cannot leak
  a setgid bit into the recorded directory mode.
- Add debian/xrpld.lintian-overrides for the deliberate /usr/local/bin/rippled
  compatibility symlink, which lintian rejects under Policy 9.1.2.
- Retry a 429 upload in publish_pkg.py: it is Nexus asking to slow down, not
  a rejection.

title: fix: Reinforce the priority of AMMClawback in case of insufficient reserves
body:
## Summary

`AMMClawback` reuses `AMMWithdraw`'s helpers to return the paired asset to the holder. When the paired asset's trustline or MPToken has to be auto-created, the holder's owner reserve was checked against `max(issuer pre-fee balance, holder current balance)` — the issuer's balance leaks into the comparison because `sfAccount` on an `AMMClawback` is the issuer. As a result the clawback failed with `tecINSUFFICIENT_RESERVE` whenever neither the issuer nor the holder could cover the extra owner reserve, even though clawback is a compliance operation that should not be blocked by a reserve requirement. A holder could also deliberately veto a clawback by deleting the paired trustline/MPToken and keeping a low spendable balance.

## Fix

Gated behind the `fixCleanup3_4_0` amendment. A new `ReserveHandling` enum is threaded through the withdraw helpers: `AMMClawback` passes `ReserveHandling::IgnoreReserve` so the owner-reserve check is skipped, while `AMMWithdraw` passes `ReserveHandling::EnforceReserve` and its behavior is unchanged. Clawback takes precedence over the reserve requirement.

## Tests

`testClawbackBypassesReserve` in `AMMClawback_test` (IOU paired asset) and `AMMClawbackMPT_test` (MPT paired asset) cover both paths:

- amendment enabled → the clawback succeeds and the paired holding is created for the holder, even though neither the issuer nor the holder can cover the extra owner reserve.
- amendment disabled → legacy behavior preserved: the transaction fails with `tecINSUFFICIENT_RESERVE` and no paired holding is created.

Both tests also assert that a plain `AMMWithdraw` under the same conditions still fails with `tecINSUFFICIENT_RESERVE`, confirming the bypass is scoped to clawback.

title: fix: PermissionedDEX (CreateOffer/Payment) never deletes expired credentials
body:
<!--
This PR template helps you to write a good pull request description.
Please feel free to include additional useful information even beyond what is requested below.

If your branch is on a personal fork and has a name that allows it to
run CI build/test jobs (e.g. "ci/foo"), remember to rename it BEFORE
opening the PR.  This avoids unnecessary redundant test runs. Renaming
the branch after opening the PR will close the PR.
https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-branches-in-your-repository/renaming-a-branch
-->

## High Level Overview of Change

The PermissionedDEX code paths (CreateOffer and Payment) check credential validity via `accountInDomain()` in PermissionedDEXHelpers.cpp, but this function uses a ReadView — making it architecturally impossible to delete expired credential SLEs from the ledger. Expired credentials persist indefinitely, locking owner reserves and causing permanent ledger bloat.

### Root Cause

The XRPL uses a two-phase cleanup pattern for expired credentials:

1. `preclaim()` (ReadView): identifies expired credentials, suppresses tecEXPIRED to allow doApply() to run

2. `doApply()` (ApplyView): calls verifyValidDomain() → removeExpired() → deleteSLE() to actually delete the expired credential from the ledger

This pattern is correctly implemented in VaultDeposit (via enforceMPTokenAuthorization → verifyValidDomain → removeExpired). However, the PermissionedDEX paths skip this entirely:

* `accountInDomain()` (PermissionedDEXHelpers.cpp:28-55) takes a ReadView const& parameter. It calls `credentials::checkExpired()` to skip expired credentials, but cannot call deleteSLE() because ReadView is immutable.

* Neither `CreateOffer::doApply()` nor `Payment::doApply()` have any call to `verifyValidDomain()` or `removeExpired()` for the PermissionedDEX credential check path.

## High Level Overview of Change
Fixes an AMMClawback boundary case where a requested clawback amount maps to exactly all of the holder’s LP tokens.

<!--
Please include a summary of the changes.

Previously, AMMClawback::equalWithdrawMatchingOneAmount() only took the full-clawback path when `lpTokensWithdraw > holdLPtokens` If the computed LP token amount was exactly equal to the holder’s LP token balance, the code fell through to the partial-withdraw path, which could fail with `tecAMM_BALANCE` in last-holder rounding scenarios.

title: fix: Remove `explicit` from std/boost hash specialisation default constructors
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Remove the `explicit` keyword from the defaulted default constructor of five `std::hash<T>` / `boost::hash<T>` specialisations in `libxrpl`:

- `std::hash<xrpl::MPTID>` (`include/xrpl/protocol/MPTIssue.h`)
- `std::hash<xrpl::MPTIssue>`, `std::hash<xrpl::Asset>` (`include/xrpl/protocol/Book.h`)
- `boost::hash<xrpl::MPTIssue>`, `boost::hash<xrpl::Asset>` (`include/xrpl/protocol/Book.h`)
- `boost::hash<::beast::ip::Address>` (`include/xrpl/beast/net/IPAddress.h`)

No behavioural change; this aligns them with the convention already used by every other hash specialisation in the codebase (`std::hash<xrpl::uint256>`, `std::hash<xrpl::Currency>`, `std::hash<xrpl::NodeID>`, `std::hash<xrpl::Directory>`, `std::hash<xrpl::AccountID>`, and the two `std::hash<xrpl::Issue>` / `std::hash<xrpl::Book>` variants).

### Context of Change

Both `std::hash<T>` and `boost::hash<T>` are required by their respective specifications to satisfy the *Hash* requirements, which include `Cpp17DefaultConstructible`. That requirement mandates the type be default-constructible in copy-initialisation contexts (i.e. `T u{};` and `T v = {};` must be well-formed), not just direct-initialisation.

Marking the defaulted default constructor `explicit` violates this: it makes copy/value-initialisation ill-formed while direct-init (`T{}` as a prvalue expression, `T()` as an operand) still compiles. This is why the bug was latent -- most direct call sites `std::hash<T>{}(x)` are direct-init and work either way. It only bites when a hasher is value-initialised inside a standard/boost library internal that lives in a copy-initialisation context, for example:

- libstdc++'s `_Hashtable_ebo_helper<_Hash>::_M_hash{}` inside a defaulted constructor of `_Hash_code_base`.
